title: "Week 7: Where You Live Is Your Health"

## Theme: Legal, Physical & Social Determinants: Environmental Justice
and Zoning

Industrial zoning is not random. Historically, hazardous facilities were
sited near communities with the least political power. This week we use
EPA EJScreen data, buffer analysis, and spatial joins to identify
residential clusters at highest risk of lead exposure. We examine the
legal doctrine of \'police power\' and two landmark health policy
studies: the Oregon Medicaid experiment and the Clean Air Act\'s
long-term consequences for children\'s earnings.

## Classroom Lab Demonstration

**Legal Focus:** Police power doctrine and its use to justify zoning
regulations; NEPA (National Environmental Policy Act) environmental
impact assessment requirements; Clean Air Act enforcement history;
Justice40 Initiative requiring 40% of federal environmental investment
to flow to disadvantaged communities.

**Health Focus:** Cumulative environmental burden --- the compounding of
multiple environmental hazards (air pollution, proximity to industrial
sites, lack of greenspace) in the same neighborhoods --- and its
relationship to lead exposure, asthma, and childhood developmental
outcomes.

**Data:** EPA EJScreen Environmental Justice Mapping Tool
(ejscreen.epa.gov --- download data or use API); Franklin County
municipal zoning shapefile (provided on Carmen from county GIS portal);
CDC Social Vulnerability Index 2020 (atsdr.cdc.gov/placeandhealth/svi);
HMDA Ohio mortgage data (ffiec.cfpb.gov/hmda).

**R Code:** QGIS: Buffer tool (Vector \> Geoprocessing Tools \> Buffer)
at 500m around industrial parcels; Vector \> Data Management \> Join
attributes by location. R: sf::st_buffer(); sf::st_join();
dplyr::summarise() to count residential parcels and population within
buffers; ggplot2 choropleth of compound vulnerability scores.

- Import EPA EJScreen data for Franklin County into QGIS; map cumulative
  environmental burden index by census tract

- Import municipal zoning shapefile; create 500m buffers around all
  industrial-zoned parcels using QGIS Buffer tool

- Perform spatial join to identify residential parcels and school
  locations within high-risk industrial buffers

- Join with CDC SVI in R to calculate compound vulnerability scores for
  exposed populations; produce choropleth map

- Load Ohio HMDA subset; compute loan denial rates by race and census
  tract; map overlaid with EJScreen burden index
